steps.text: Mix together the white sugar and water in a small saucepan over high heat and bring to a boil; boil for one minute. Remove from heat and stir in the peanut butter until melted well blended. Pour the warm sauce over ice cream to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Peanut Butter Ice Cream Topping
raw_recipe.description: What a quick and fun alternative to bottled and jarred sauces from the store! Wow your guests with this home made peanut butter ice cream topping on your sundae bar.
raw_recipe.name: Peanut Butter Ice Cream Topping

recipeInstructions.text: Mix together the white sugar and water in a small saucepan over high heat and bring to a boil; boil for one minute. Remove from heat and stir in the peanut butter until melted well blended. Pour the warm sauce over ice cream to serve.

review.reviewBody: I went with VOODOOMISS's suggestion & made this recipe with 1/3 c. sugar, 1/3 c water, then 2/3 c. pb. After I stirred to blend, I just used a whisk to fluff it up. Turned out exactly how i wanted it to.

I used 1/2 cup whole milk instead of water & 1/2 cup sugar with 1/2 cup peanut butter. While I trying to create a thicker consistency by whipping with hand held mixers I also ADDED a teaspoon vanilla. It was perfect. Definitely sweet.

I made this using 1/2 cup milk, 1/2 cup sugar, 2/3 cup peanut butter and 1 tsp vanilla. I boiled the milk and sugar for 1 minute stirring constantly, turned off heat , added vanilla, peanut butter and whisked until the consistency of caramel. Used this to make Peanut Butter Lava Brownies. (Bake Brownie cupcakes, turn upside down, make small well in center of brownie and fill with Peanut Butter Lava and have running over sides of brownie. 5*****, "Money" and "Fire" were my families comments.

I am definitely going to try this recipe. There were many comments on the grainy consistency. I will make a simple syrup using 1/2 cup water and 1/2 cup sugar. Bring to boil and reduce heat while stirring to completely dissolve the sugar. Then add 1 cup peanut butter, a small amount of butter (for sheen) and a bit of vanilla. Whisk with hand blender (whisk attachment), or whatever means you have to blend till smooth.
It was delicious! I used 1/3 c water, 1/3 c sugar and 2/3 c Jif creamy peanut butter. Stirred with a whisk - consistency was great!

Follow the third cup water and sugar with two thirds peanut butter alteration. Came out great that way although a touch runny. 

Also I put the sugar and water in a glass bowl in the microwave, heated and stirred to dissolve sugar then added peanut butter and whipped it, worked fine took 5 minutes to make start to finish.

I made it with 1/2 cup water/sugar, then 1 Cup Jif peanut butter. Used a hand held mixer to make it smooth.
Very tasty and much better than Dairy Queen's p.b. topping!

I searched for a peanut butter type filling or frosting using a limited source of ingreadients, So I made this adding a teaspoone of hot fudge to get a more setup finish. Then using a pipeing bag I injected it into my chocolate cake batter and finally drizzled it over the finished cake. Awesome just what I needed for a recovering alcoholics monster sweet tooth!!:)

I followed the advice of others. I used 1/3 cup water, 1/3 cup sugar and 1 cup peanutbutter. After I stirred the ingredients I added 1 tablespoon butter and a 1/2 tsp of vanilla. It was velvety smooth and delicious!

Eh, not so great. I have a *major* sweet tooth and as is, the recipe is wayy too sweet. I ended up doubling the peanut butter and adding a pinch or two of salt to cut the sweetness. The texture was also a mess. I stirred it with a wooden spoon and tried a whisk but with no luck. I ended up having to dump it all in the blender and give it a healthy whirl. This is a recipe with room for improvement.
I made this like the other comments suggested, 1/3 c sugar, 1/3 c water, 2/3 cup peanut butter. It was really delicious! It tastes like our favorite ice cream place.
My Aunt Helen had a frozen custard shop in the 60's, she made this all the time. Yummmmmmmmm

I honestly don't even know how to rate this recipe. I followed the directions exactly and wanted to save it for when my family comes over. However, it separated almost immediately after putting it in a container. I whisked it again to mix it thinking perhaps I had not mixed it well enough. It separated again. It does taste good but I'm disappointed that it keeps separating. Any suggestions for how to improve this would be greatly appreciated.
Per other comments I made it as follows. 1/3 cup sugar, 1/3 cup milk and 2/3 cup peanut butter.
Far too sweet for me, even with double the peanut butter.
Yum! I followed VooDoo Miss's recommendations of 1/3 water, 1/3 sugar and 2/3 c peanut butter. I had some chocolate ice cream I wanted to put it on. Thanks for the easy recipe!
Love it!!!

This was ok, but if you are seeking something closer to the Friendly’s topping I reccommend this instead: use all natural peanut butter (this is important for the right texture and flavor. Most grocery stores have various brands)). I usually start with 1/2 cup; mix in a small amount of peanut oil (add about a tablespoon at a time and stir to combine after each addition until you get a consistency that is still thick but can be poured). Once it’s the desired consistency add powdered sugar, again by tablespoon, mixing after each addition, until it is sweetened slightly or to your preference. Note: if the addition of powdered sugar thickens the sauce too much simply add a bit more peanut oil and stir until it’s pouring consistency. Any left over can be stored in an airtight container in a cupboard for a few days.

Followed other reviewers by using 1/3 cup sugar, 1/3 cup water and 2/3 cups peanut butter. So quick and easy to make and crazy good. I'm going to use it as the swirl in my homemade pb ice cream this afternoon once ice cream mixture chills a little longer in fridge. Also going to add Reese pb morsels. I'm trying to re-create, or at least come close to, Publix's Greenwise PB Trinity Ice Cream. Fun!

I too doubled the peanut butter, though for my tastes it could have used even more. It looked a bit curdled until I took a whisk to it and it started to cool, then it smoothed out beautifully. I think the instructions may just be a bit incomplete
